approved: Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder Commission of Inquiry Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a parliamentary inquiry into the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder's conduct and results.
The inquiry would have the same powers as a Royal Commission, such as summoning witnesses and demanding documents, but would be set up by Parliament rather than the government.
The inquiry would report to Parliament with proposals to improve trust and openness in Murray-Darling Basin water management.
Establishes a Commission of Inquiry into the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder.
Gives the Commission powers equal to a Royal Commission, including to compel witnesses and require documents.
Requires the Commission to report to Parliament with findings and recommendations.
The Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder, agricultural producers, regional economies, and communities in the Murray-Darling Basin.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders so a bill establishing a commission of inquiry into the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder could be presented, debated and advanced without delay; argued that scrutiny was needed to examine environmental water management, transparency, governance, outcomes and effects on Murray-Darling Basin communities, agriculture and regional economies.
Moved that the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder Commission of Inquiry Bill 2026 be called on immediately for debate until the end of private senators' bills time; the question was agreed to.
